keyframe_review.note: 0.259 M km2: al-Hira on the Euphrates and the desert to the south-west, to the head of the Gulf (Iraq, Kuwait, the north of Saudi Arabia; bbox 39.9-48.2 E, 27.7-33.3 N). The page: 'ruled parts of Southern Mesopotamia and northeastern Arabia'; it gives no area. The shape holds the settled core, not the claims: al-Tabari places Imru' al-Qays I's rule 'in all the land of the Arabs in Iraq, Hejaz and Mesopotamia' and the Namara epitaph has him at Najran (Imru' al-Qays page, undated), and Mundhir III's raids reached Syria and 'Najd southward' (Mundhir III page); those are not drawn. The 270 start is Cliopatria's; the page has the kingdom 'Established: c. 293' and its table starts 'Amr I ibn Adi in 268. Re-read 2026-10-19 (thin items): the Namara inscription page dates the epitaph of Imru' al-Qays to AD 328 ('dated securely'), with him 'king of the Arabs' who 'subdued the Asadis', 'subdued Ma'add', 'put to flight Madhhij' and drove enemies 'to the gates of Najran'; Hejaz and Mesopotamia are not in its text (they are al-Tabari's words on the Imru' al-Qays page). That is tribal overlordship, not a holding the pages map, so nothing is drawn. The Al-Hirah page has 'Over the sixth century, Al-Hira ruled over Ma'add' (central Arabia), Bahrain only as a caravan route, and no mention of Yamama, Najd or Ain Tamr.

wars.name: Lakhmid raids on Roman Syria in the Iberian War
wars.outcome: Al-Mundhir III ravaged Syria in 526 and 528 (capturing two Roman commanders in 526) and in 529 took the Khabour frontier area and marched towards Nisibis, Apamea and Chalcedon but could not take Antioch; no border moved.
wars.note: The page says the Byzantine-Sasanian war began in 526 and that Mundhir attacked Syria during it; the eastern limit of the raids was the Euphrates.

wars.name: Lakhmid-Ghassanid wars
wars.outcome: Al-Mundhir III 'defeated the Ghassanids at the famous Battle of Callinicum in 531 AD' (Lakhmid page) and was killed fighting al-Harith ibn Jabalah's Ghassanids at Yawm Halima in June 554 (Mundhir III page). The Lakhmids, a Sasanian client state, opposed the Ghassanids, Rome's Arab clients (page, paraphrased); neither battle changed a border on the pages opened.
wars.note: No contest zone is drawn: the pages give no ground held or taken.

wars.name: Deposition of al-Nu'man III and the Battle of Dhi Qar
wars.outcome: Khosrow II seized al-Nu'man III at Ctesiphon in 602 and ended the kingdom; the Banu Bakr then beat a Persian force with Arab auxiliaries under Iyas ibn Qabisah at Dhi Qar in southern Iraq ('between 604 and 611 AD'; Muslim traditions 602-624), 'may have been no more than a skirmish'.
wars.note: After the end of the kingdom; the page does not say what happened to al-Hira afterwards. [Reviewer me-06-d, 2026-10-19: clipped from 602-611 to the kingdom's life (ends 602); Dhi Qar (604-611) falls after the end]

notes:
Written by me-06-d on 2026-10-19 from five pages (the page budget for 8 shapes). The infobox of the Lakhmid page gives no area.

ROW TO FIX: Cliopatria's Lakhmid row (270-601, then 629-633) has a gap of 602-628, which the Sasanian shape fills (the sasanian-empire dossier gains the land in 602), and a reappearance in 629-633. The page ends the kingdom in 602 and has Persian governors in Hira to 633 (the rulers table lists Iyas ibn Qabisah with Nakhiragan to 617/618 and Azadbeh 617/618-633 as the table's last rulers, which is probably why Cliopatria runs the row to 633). The 629 and 633 shapes are therefore marked wrong and this dossier ends in 602. ACTION FOR THE SASANIAN DOSSIER: its keyframes 629-633 do not contain these cells (0 shared cells with Cliopatria's Sasanian shapes of 629, 630 and 633), so without a union with {cliopatria: Lakhmid Kingdom, year: 629} (and a loss to rashidun-caliphate at Hira in May 633) the land of al-Hira is in nobody's dossier in 629-633. The sasanian-empire dossier (me-06-c) is complete and not mine to edit.

START: three dates on one page: the table's 'Amr I 268, the text's c. 293-302 and the infobox's c. 293; Cliopatria starts in 270 and the dossier keeps 270 (found event at confidence 1). No predecessor is named on the page (infobox: not stated); the land is the south-western Sasanian march and the Arab desert, so predecessors is empty.

NOT DRAWN: the claims of Imru' al-Qays I (Najran, Hejaz, 'all the land of the Arabs in Iraq, Hejaz and Mesopotamia') and Mundhir III's raids (Syria, Najd southward) have no dated holding on the pages; Bahrain, Yamama and Kindah are not on any page opened, although the gazetteer has 'Bahrain (historical)' and 'Nejd'. Cliopatria's group note says it lacks Kindah and the Hejaz towns; those belong to a separate dossier (me-06-x).

INTERLUDES WITHOUT A BORDER MOVE: the non-dynastic kings (Aws ibn Qallam 363-368; Abu Ya'fur 503-505), the Persian governor Suhrab (573-574) and the 'more formal subordinates' wording for the sixth century are in the table only; no event is written for them. The Sasanian dossier records the client relation (vassal_start 270, vassal_end 602) with counterpart lakhmid-kingdom.

COUNTERPARTS: Banu Bakr (a tribal confederation, Dhi Qar) is named in one war and has no Cliopatria row.

DISAGREEMENT: the reviewer proposed confidence 2 for the 270 start; I kept 1, because 270 is Cliopatria's year and the page's own dates are c. 293 and later (Lakhmid page infobox 'Established: c. 293'), so no page dates the vassalage to 270. (2) The found region is now the intersection of the Kufa disc with Cliopatria's Lakhmid shape of 270 (114 cells; checked with tools/gazetteer.py: the disc is 270 cells, 156 of them Sasanian). (3) /wars/3 (to 602) was clipped by the reviewer and is left as set. (4) Thin items tried: the Namara inscription page dates Imru' al-Qays I's epitaph to AD 328 and names Asad, Ma'add, Madhhij and Najran (tribal overlordship, not drawn); the Al-Hirah page dates nothing for Bahrain, Yamama or Najd (Ma'add ruled over the sixth century). Found 270 stays at confidence 1.
